GENERAL SCIENCE — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters.? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Skeletal and Muscular System? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Skeletal and Muscular System.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Skeletal and Muscular System.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Skeletal and Muscular System.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Skeletal and Muscular System.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Polymers? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Polymers.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Polymers.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Polymers.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Polymers.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell division? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell division.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell division.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell division.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cell division.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.

   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics.

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

15. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

17. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

   B. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution and Biodiversity.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution and Biodiversity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution and Biodiversity.

21. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrolysis? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrolysis.
